topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
consensus_response: Increasing the array size in SIW arrays for high-gain inter-satellite antennas can improve gain and angular coverage, but also leads to higher insertion loss due to increased SIW line length. To maintain efficiency, hybrid feeding topology can be optimized, and advanced substrate materials can be used to reduce transmission line loss per unit length. This balance allows for larger arrays, enhancing gain, while minimizing insertion loss, leading to more efficient designs. However, increased complexity of the feeding network with larger arrays may lead to increased manufacturing costs and potential losses in efficiency due to the increased number of connections.
reference_context: The reference context discusses the design and implementation of a wideband high-gain high-efficiency hybrid integrated plate array antenna for V-band inter-satellite links. The antenna consists of microstrip patches, substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and waveguide power dividers. The radiation efficiency of SIW arrays with different sizes is compared by experiment, and the hybrid SIW waveguide feeding topology is optimized to realize high efficiency, low cost and compact configuration at the same time.
